observations.source_name: Smithsonian / USGS Weekly Volcanic Activity Report
observations.title: Kanlaon volcano (Philippines)
observations.description: The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) reported continuing eruptive activity at Kanlaon during 7-14 October. The seismic network recorded 0-19 daily volcanic earthquakes and during 11-13 October 5-6 daily periods of volcanic tremor lasting 2-64 minutes. In general, sulfur dioxide emissions ranged from 932 to 3,219 tonnes per day (t/d), though a peak of 4,656 t/d was recorded on 10 October, the same day as a larger eruptive event. Moderate-to-voluminous volcanic emissions generally rose as high as 1.2 km above the summit and drifted in various directions. A moderately explosive eruption at 1246 on 10 October produced an ash plume that rose 5-6 km above the summit and drifted NNE. The event lasted for two minutes, though ash emissions were recorded for two hours and 41 minutes. The Office of Civil Defense - Negros Island Region (OCD-NIR) reported that residents of Bago City observed the ash plume, heard booming sounds, and felt the ground shake. A sulfur odor was reported in parts of barangay Codcod in San Carlos City. Ashfall and a sulfur odor were reported in barangay Ara-al, Gintubdan, and in the barangays Igmayaan, Bunga, Bacong, Kumaliskis, Bago, and Pandanon, in Don Salvador Benedicto, based also on a news report. Residents of La Carlota City heard rumbling. On 11 October a total of 10 ash emissions lasting 11 minutes to three hours and 33 minutes generated ash plumes that rose as high as 600 m above the summit and drifted NNW, NW, and W. Several of the events were visible in webcam images; at 0318 minor Strombolian activity produced an ash plume that rose 500 m above the summit and drifted WNW. At 0000 and during 0545-0724 on 12 October ash plumes rose 300 m above the crater rim and drifted NW. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 0-5); the public was warned to stay out of the 4-km-radius Permanent Danger Zone (PDZ) and pilots were advised to avoid flying close to the summit. Sources: Inquirer.net,Office of Civil Defense, Republic of the Philippines,Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS)
